answer: Each identity in an agent economy keeps a unique 6 GB dataset generated from its public key and listed at a vertex in a public registry, so no two identities hold the same blocks. Random auditors hourly demand 48 named blocks; a failed reply writes a plume flag next to that identity's relic record on the public log, and two flags in one epoch end its eligibility. Keeping one dataset costs an honest agent 6 GB once. Running 1,000 identities costs 6 TB held continuously and 1,000 separate audit replies, since blocks from one dataset never match the coordinates of another.
